sections.h2: Five EPA-run models put corn-ethanol land-use change between −0.95 and about 41 gCO₂e/MJ

chart.title: The five models disagree by tens of grams of CO₂e per megajoule
chart.sub: Land-use-change GHG estimate for corn ethanol, gCO₂e/MJ.

sections.means: ADAGE's run implies land-use change was a net carbon sink at −0.95 gCO₂e/MJ, while the high end across the five frameworks reached roughly 41 gCO₂e/MJ.

sections.h2: Land-protection choices alone shift the GCAM-T result by 7 to 11 gCO₂e/MJ

chart.title: Same model and scenario: land protection moves the result by 19% to 32%
chart.sub: Change in land-use-change carbon intensity against the baseline GCAM-T variant, gCO₂e/MJ.
chart.source: Peer-reviewed land-representation study on GCAM v5.1.2 (PMC9132210).

sections.means: Changing only how much non-commercial land is protected moved the estimate by 7 gCO₂e/MJ (19%) and by 11 gCO₂e/MJ (32%).
sections.todo: Report the land-protection assumption alongside any GCAM-based carbon-intensity figure.

sections.h2: EU transport biofuels must clear a GHG-savings bar that depends on plant start date

chart.title: Plants started from 2021 must save 65%, against 50% for the oldest plants
chart.sub: Minimum GHG savings for transport biofuels under RED II/RED III, %.
chart.source: IEA and ICCT summaries of the EU Renewable Energy Directive.

sections.means: A transport biofuel either clears the threshold for its plant's start date or it does not, with no traded credit involved.
